title: Tapping Domain Residual Integrity Audit
objective: Determine whether a genuinely unresolved, user-visible, data-integrity, provenance, projection, or generated-artifact risk remains in the tapping domain after T1-T12.

silent_drop_audit.finding: All 4 tap-type-classification-consuming validators (validate-tapping-atlas.js, validate-tap-type-guide.js, validate-tapping-workflow.js, validate-tapping-evidence.js) hardcode the same fixed list of 4 classification field names (general_taxonomy, manufacturing_characteristics, typical_applications, manufacturer_specific_recommendations) rather than dynamically enumerating whatever classification arrays the tap-type projection row actually contains. Confirmed via direct source inspection of all 4 files. Current tap-types.json rows contain exactly these 4 fields plus entity_id/title/taxonomy_axis/definition/evidence_status metadata -- no field is silently dropped TODAY. But if the projection schema ever gained a 5th classification field (a realistic future extension, since general_taxonomy itself was added this way via the T3 correction), no validator would notice a consumer failing to render it.
silent_drop_audit.severity_relative_to_selected_target: Lower priority than the selected target: this is a forward-looking architectural fragility with zero current live impact, versus the selected target which is a present-tense, unverified trust claim about data that is displayed to users today.
silent_drop_audit.not_selected_reason: Ranking criteria (correctness risk, trust/provenance risk) favor a live, present-tense gap over a hypothetical future one. Recorded here for future reference, not selected as the T13 target.

findings.exact_source_field: hole_preparation.cross_verified (an object present only on the 9 cross-checked metric records; hp.status itself is 'verified' on all 29 records knowledge-layer-wide and is explicitly NOT the source of this derivation, per the generator's own code comment)
findings.semantic_correctness_of_rule_as_written: INCOMPLETE -- the rule only checks that hp.cross_verified is truthy (present), never that hp.cross_verified.match is true. The source schema DOES carry a `match` boolean on every cross_verified object observed (confirmed present and true on all 9 current records), meaning the schema anticipates a cross-check that could find a mismatch. If a future data-acquisition phase ever recorded a genuine mismatch (cross_verified present, match: false), the current derivation would still mark that record 'verified' -- incorrect. This exact class of bug (deriving from presence of the wrong signal rather than its actual value) is what T3's own historical correction was about, one layer up the pipeline (application_notes classification, not this field).
findings.evidence: grep across scripts/validators/ for any validator that both reads data/datasets/{metric,unc,unf}_tapping.seed.json's hole_preparation.cross_verified field AND cross-checks it against data/projections/tapping/tapping-profiles.json's tap_drill.status returns zero results. validate-tapping-projections.js check 4 ('Verification-State Correctness') only confirms tap_drill.status is a member of the 4-value enum -- it never looks at the source dataset at all. validate-tapping-domain.js operates entirely within the knowledge/dataset layer and checks hp.status (always 'verified', by design, per T1's convention) -- it never reads hp.cross_verified either.
findings.current_live_data_note: All 9 records currently marked tap_drill.status='verified' do have cross_verified present with match:true; all 5 metric fine-pitch + 8 UNC + 7 UNF records marked 'source_bound' have cross_verified absent. The 9/20 split displayed everywhere today is factually correct for the CURRENT data -- confirmed by direct inspection of all three tapping dataset seed files. The risk is entirely about the absence of a REGRESSION GUARD, not a live defect.

findings.semantic_correctness_of_rule_as_written: correct -- a pass-through, not a computation; no multi-field logic to get wrong

entity.application_notes[].status (authored directly on each knowledge-layer entity record)

findings.semantic_correctness_of_rule_as_written: correct -- a straightforward count of an already-authoritative per-note field, not a reinterpretation of a proxy signal

status_derivation_audit.conclusion: Exactly one derived-status field (tap_drill.status) has an untested derivation rule that reads a proxy signal (presence of hp.cross_verified) rather than the full available signal (hp.cross_verified.match), and no validator anywhere re-derives it from source to confirm correctness. This is the selected T13 target.

provenance_derivation_audit.findings: No new fabrication/fallback risk found beyond what T11 already hardened. verificationLabel() functions are identical pure mappings (verified->'Verified', source_bound->'Source-bound', etc.) across all consumers, not fallback-prone. The one narrative-text field worth flagging is tap_drill.provenance.cross_check, which is a GENERATED STRING (`Matches ${hp.cross_verified.table} exactly (verified ${hp.cross_verified.verified_date})`) built from the same crossVerified boolean as the status derivation above -- if that boolean is ever wrong, this narrative text would also incorrectly claim an exact match. This is the same root cause as the status-derivation finding, not a separate risk; folded into the same T13 target rather than treated as new.

static_client_parity_audit.comparison: reference/tapping-atlas.html (static) vs tools/tapping-workflow.html + reference/tapping-evidence.html (client-side, shared js/tapping-workflow-data.js data file) vs reference/tap-type-guide.html (static)
static_client_parity_audit.finding: No material fact/value/status/provenance/classification/standard-identity divergence found across consumers for the same projection row. validate-tapping-workflow.js explicitly checks tap_drill.status equality between the embedded data file and the projection (line 58-59); T11 extended this class of check to full provenance objects. Since Atlas, Guide, Workflow, and Evidence all read directly from the same two projection files with no independent re-derivation of their own, and every consumer's fidelity to the projection is independently checked, parity is CERTIFIED for every family in the matrix except C/E, whose divergence risk (if any) would appear identically in every consumer simultaneously (since it originates upstream of all of them, at the projection-generation step) -- not a parity gap between consumers, but a shared correctness gap in the single upstream source they all trust equally.

generator_artifact_staleness_audit.finding: No automated staleness-detection mechanism exists anywhere in the repository (no build manifest, no source-checksum-to-artifact linkage, no CI). Every phase (T1-T12) has manually run each generator and manually recorded/compared SHA-256 checksums as part of its own audit discipline -- this has worked reliably across 12 phases with zero drift incidents recorded, but it is a process discipline, not a mechanically enforced invariant. This mirrors the T12-discovery-session finding that no persisted site-wide QA validator exists either.
generator_artifact_staleness_audit.reason_not_selected: Section 7 of the phase brief explicitly frames this as audit-only ('This is an audit, not a request to redesign the build system'), and fixing it would require build-system-level changes far broader than a single bounded validator addition -- fails the 'minimal architectural disruption' and 'bounded file scope' selection criteria.

risk_ranking.user_visible_consequence: The literal claim '9 verified tap-drill values' (displayed on every product) would be silently wrong if the derivation ever regressed or a future record legitimately had cross_verified present with match:false.

risk_ranking.implementation_scope: one new check in validate-tapping-projections.js; no generator or product change required, since current live data already satisfies the correct rule

selected_t13_target.title: Tap-Drill Status Source-to-Projection Derivation Verification
selected_t13_target.objective: Add a validator check that independently re-derives the expected tap_drill.status for every profile directly from the source dataset's hole_preparation.cross_verified field (using the correct rule -- present AND match !== false) and confirms it matches the projection's actual tap_drill.status, closing the one seam in the tapping pipeline where no validator compares projection output back to its knowledge-layer source.
selected_t13_target.root_risk: generate-tapping-projections.js's buildTapDrillBlock() derives tap_drill.status from Boolean(hp.cross_verified) alone, ignoring the cross_verified.match sub-field the schema already carries. No validator anywhere re-derives this from source and compares. Current live data happens to be correct (verified by direct inspection), but nothing would catch a future regression or a legitimately-recorded mismatch.
selected_t13_target.source_of_truth: data/datasets/metric_tapping.seed.json, data/datasets/unc_tapping.seed.json, data/datasets/unf_tapping.seed.json -- specifically each record's hole_preparation.cross_verified object (or its absence) and, if present, its .match boolean
selected_t13_target.affected_consumers: data/projections/tapping/tapping-profiles.json (tap_drill.status field); indirectly every downstream product that displays it
selected_t13_target.existing_coverage: validate-tapping-projections.js check 4 (enum-membership only); validate-tapping-domain.js (source-dataset-internal checks only, never cross-referenced against the projection)
selected_t13_target.coverage_gap: no check reads BOTH the source dataset's cross_verified.match AND the projection's tap_drill.status and compares them per matching record
selected_t13_target.validator_behavior_required: For each of the 29 tapping_profile_id values, locate the corresponding source dataset record (across metric_tapping/unc_tapping/unf_tapping), compute expectedStatus = (hp.cross_verified && hp.cross_verified.match !== false) ? 'verified' : 'source_bound', and fail if it doesn't equal the projection row's tap_drill.status.
selected_t13_target.mutation_test_required: In a disposable copy of one dataset seed file, temporarily set an existing verified record's hole_preparation.cross_verified.match to false (or delete cross_verified entirely) without regenerating the projection; run the new check against the now-inconsistent source+projection pair; confirm it fails. Restore and confirm pass.
selected_t13_target.false_positive_test_required: Run the new check against the real, current, untouched source datasets and projection; must pass with 0 errors, since current data is already correct.
selected_t13_target.pass_criteria: 0 errors against real data; correctly fails against the reproduced mismatch; all 9 existing tapping validators continue to pass; all regression checksums remain byte-identical (this is validator-only, no generator or product change is needed since current data already satisfies the correct rule).
selected_t13_target.bounded_file_scope: scripts/validators/validate-tapping-projections.js only (the natural home -- it already loads the knowledge layer and cross-references it against the projection).

implementation.check_added: Tap-Drill Status Correctly Derived From Source Cross-Verification
implementation.mechanism: For each of the 29 tapping_profile_id values, locates the matching source record across metric_tapping/unc_tapping/unf_tapping via knowledge.datasetById, computes expectedStatus = (hp.cross_verified && hp.cross_verified.match !== false) ? 'verified' : 'source_bound', and fails if it disagrees with the projection row's actual tap_drill.status.
